rationales.A: Image 1 shows a single walled compound on the St. Lawrence River: a fortified post with cannons at the corners, a flag flying, chimneys smoking, and a garden beside it. Background: there is no town and no farmland around it — the Habitation was a trading post where a few Frenchmen exchanged goods with Native peoples for furs. A grid city is what Image 2 shows, sugar plantations belong to the West Indies, and no church or school is visible here.
rationales.B: A grid city is what Image 2 shows, not the Habitation.
rationales.C: Sugar plantations belong to the West Indies, not to Quebec.
rationales.D: No church or school is visible in the engraving.
rationales.general:
1. Look at Image 1. One walled compound on the river, with cannons and a flag.
2. Ask what is missing. No town, no streets, no farmland around it.
3. Name the place. A trading post — a few men, a fort, and the fur trade.
4. Drop the rest. The grid city is Image 2, sugar belongs to the West Indies, and no church is shown.
Remember: read the picture before you read the options — the image is the evidence.

stem: What does the Habitation engraving (Image 1) most directly show about New France?

stimulus.source_note: Image 1: Samuel de Champlain, Habitation at Quebec, from Les Voyages (1613), public domain. Image 2: Castello Plan of New Amsterdam in 1660, redrawn 1916 by John Wolcott Adams for I. N. Phelps Stokes, public domain.
stimulus.text: Two images of European colonies in North America. Image 1: Samuel de Champlain's engraving of the Habitation at Quebec, from his Les Voyages (1613). A single walled and fortified post stands on the St. Lawrence River, with cannons at the corners, a flag flying, chimneys smoking, and a garden beside it — one compound, with no town and no farms around it. Image 2: The Castello Plan of New Amsterdam in 1660, redrawn in 1916 by John Wolcott Adams for I. N. Phelps Stokes. A bird's-eye view of a whole town at the tip of Manhattan, with a fort, a wall across the island, canals, streets of houses with gardens, and ships in the harbor.
